appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus praises him — « c'est un si brave homme que Brichot », « un homme d'une grande valeur » — but the narrator at once notes « qu'en son absence, il ne se gênait pas pour dauber sur lui », calls his talk something « que le moins raffiné des convives de Mme de Guermantes eût trouvé si bête et si lourd », shows him trading on the baron as a curiosity for bourgeois friends (« le descendant des Condé »), and lets Charlus flatten him: « vous êtes ignorant comme une carpe. — Vous êtes dur, baron, mais juste. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The baron's warm testimonial is immediately undercut by the narrator, who exposes Brichot as two-faced, dull, and self-important, and then stages his outright defeat in the conversation, which he himself ratifies as deserved.

appraisal_events.evidence: « une voix piaillante », « son masque grave et enfariné », « un vieux trumeau comme moi », « j'ai plus de quarante ans, dit le baron, qui avait dépassé la soixantaine » ; the narrator's « grande et affectueuse pitié […] depuis que Mme Verdurin avait dévoilé son dessein devant moi » ; « le besoin de la confidence étant chez lui plus fort que la crainte de la divulgation » ; Brichot foresees « que le baron risquait fort d'être, de façon imminente, exclu du petit clan ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Even while Charlus holds the floor, the narrator frames him as ridiculous, self-deceiving about his age, compulsively betraying the life he tries to hide, and already marked for expulsion from the clan — a pitying diminishment the narration plainly endorses.

status_effects.explanation: He is shown to be disloyal behind Charlus's back, tediously pedantic, and vain about his Sorbonne standing, so the praise he receives reads as misplaced.
In the exchange he is corrected, called ignorant, left « stupéfait » by Charlus's figures, and concedes the point himself.
He dominates the conversation as sole authority — on reputations, on Swann and Odette, on history — schooling a Sorbonne professor who accepts the verdict.
The same talk exposes him: the powdered mask, the lie about his age, the self-betraying confidences, and the pity plus imminent exclusion the narrator attaches to him lower his local standing.

Charlus's disclosures work on him as fresh injury — « ma souffrance s'accroissait d'une souffrance nouvelle », « J'étais épouvanté par la statistique » — and he transposes the catalogue of Odette's lovers onto Albertine and his own blindness.

ambiguities: In the digression on Mme de Villeparisis a countervailing movement is left unrepresented: her family standing is revealed as greater than the narrator supposed, while the duchesse de ***'s « Cochon ! » to Doudeauville is of ambiguous target — it may mock his taste rather than disparage her.
